facts.text: Existing coverage: exo-cluster-software.md and exo-vs-mlx-launch-tensor-parallel-throughput-comparison.md already state that exo pins mlx==0.32.0 from rltakashige/mlx-jaccl-fix-small-recv branch address-rdma-gpu-locks and mlx-lm from rltakashige/mlx-lm branch leo/deepseek-v4; nothing is restated here
The fork repository page lists 8 branches, 1 tag, 1,807 commits and 8 forks, and its README is the unmodified upstream MLX README
The fork's latest visible commit is upstream's 'Fix jaccl init bug (#3418)' by angeloskath dated Apr 16 2026, so the fork carries no commit newer than that upstream state

A downstream exo fork (adurham) pinned mlx back to commit f8bac642 on May 1 2026 because upstream's JACCL barrier merge (3835dbab) uses Dtype::UInt8 and non-virtual override markers that do not compile against the exo fork's Dtype and base-class state
The same downstream merge note says exo itself did not use barrier() at that time, so reverting the barrier merge was safe for them
Every upstream mlx bump therefore needs a manual rebase of the exo fork; a 562-commit lag plus an incompatible upstream JACCL change shows the pin is not tracking MLX main

exo's lock file resolved the fork branch to commit cc3f3e6 while the fork tip e983561 'Prevent GPU timeouts' hangs test_eval_slow_fast_multi_stream with the flag on (already in mlx-metal-fast-synch dossier); a user building from the branch name instead of the lock gets a different MLX than exo ships
